title: Looking for something similar to Rosebud.AI
author: Maleficent-Soft4190
selftext:
Howdy, I'm currently looking for a ai game dev that's similar to [Rosebud.ai](http://Rosebud.ai), the issue I have with rosebud are the following:

1) I hate the predatory token system rosebud as well as many of the other ai projects use  
2) After developing my game I'd like to be able to move it to Steam, while you can do this with rosebud, it is not straightforward and rosebud has a tendency to make systems not with exporting in mind. (i.e. runs fine not exported, once exported tends to become glitchy and break)

3) Not rosebud but other ai's: I don't want to have to get a chatgpt token or anything of the sort, especially when I'm trying to just check it out to see if it works for me.

comments.author: octaviustf
comments.body: I’ve tried building an browser based 3d game generator and honestly the tech isn’t quite there yet in my experience. Just wait a few months and there will be a flood of game generators to choose from. Also try making your own game with Claude code it’s pretty fun

replies.author: Maleficent-Soft4190
replies.body: is there a specific game engine Claude works with better than others?

replies.author: swirllyman
replies.body: I've been running Claude with the Unity MCP and been getting pretty decent results. Takes a little (tiny) setup and Claude can walk you through it.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: You're going to either have to deal with a credit system or an api key, no one is giving away a meaningful amount of compute for free.

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body:
Yeah, this is accurate - hard for these platforms to subsidise free use because the cost to run game dev on AI is much, much higher than regular coding tasks - more complex and bigger projects.

Speaking from experience running one

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Yeah, I have this problem with my ai powered game, even providing a small amount of usage free per day adds up quick.

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body: Yep! It will get cheaper but right now it’s just costly token wise

comments.author: VRSportz
comments.body: Astrocade is free, but don't think it's capable of talking the next GTA. Good for little mini games and testing prototypes and mechanics

comments.author: hejwow
comments.body: Try spawn.co - not stellar but nice to work with

replies.author: Maleficent-Soft4190
replies.body: It's cool, though the fact that the games cannot be exported for uploading to places like steam is a pretty big dealbreaker for me. Thanks for the recommendation though.

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body:
Founder of [tesana.ai](http://tesana.ai) here - happy to give you some credits so you can try out the platform,

I've been posting here quite frequently sharing games and builds! Would love to have more feedback from devs
